interventions.speaker: EXPERT-EAU
interventions.who: EAU guideline specialist; speaks only from the guideline text he retrieved
interventions.body:
GUIDELINE
"Weak\nOmit biopsy and offer PSA monitoring when MRI is negative (i.e. PI-RADS ≤ 2), and clinical\nsuspicion of PCa is low (PSA density < 0.20 ng/mL/cc and no family history)."

WHAT THE EXPERTS DO NOT SETTLE
The experts are divided on the management strategy following a negative biopsy in the context of a PI-RADS 2 finding and a PSA of 1.6 ng/mL. Expert One favors continued surveillance, while Expert Five also suggests continued surveillance. The uncertainty lies in whether the clinical context (PI-RADS 2, negative biopsy) mandates immediate surveillance or if the PSA rise warrants further action despite the negative biopsy.

WHAT THE DOCUMENTS MUST SETTLE
The documents must settle the appropriate follow-up strategy: Should the patient proceed with continued surveillance, or is there an indication for further intervention given the PSA rise and the prior negative biopsy?

5.5
Biopsy strategy
Prostate biopsy can be performed using various strategies (systematic, targeted, etc.) and approaches (i.e.
transperineal versus transrectal).
5.5.1
Systematic biopsy strategy
For systematic biopsies in which no prior imaging is used for targeting, the sample sites should be bilateral from
apex to base, as far posterior and lateral as possible in the peripheral gland, regardless of the approach used. A
2006 SR showed that 12 is the minimum number of cores for systematic biopsies, with > 12 cores not increasing
cancer detection rate significantly [406].
5.5.2
Targeted biopsy strategy
Where MRI has shown a suspicious lesion, MR-targeted biopsy can be obtained through cognitive guidance, US/
MR fusion software or direct in-bore guidance.
